subject: capybara
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: capybara with a small bird on its head.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but quality rigged capybara model with a realistic scale, structuring the hierarchy with hips, a spine chain, legs, head, jaw, ears, and a tail stub, plus a separately jointed bird perched on its head.

Continuing the design: sweeping the spine chain into an elliptical body profile with countershaded fur, building a head with skull, muzzle, jaw, eyes, nose, and ears, then rigging four limbs as chains with foot details, and finally adding a small bird on the head with its own body, beak, wings, tail, legs, and eye, parented to the head joint.

I'm also adding whimsical touches like a yuzu fruit sphere near the bird and blush cheek decals, then working out ground-relative positions so the legs, body, and feet line up correctly with the floor.

For the legs, I'm setting up joint chains (hip, knee, ankle) per side with appropriate bend directions for hind versus front limbs, sweeping cylindrical segments with tapering radii. Then I'm positioning the head joint and extending the spine forward to connect the neck and head naturally to the body.

Now I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere, adding a blunt blocky muzzle box characteristic of a capybara's face, a darker nose pad, a hinged lower jaw bone, and small scaled ear spheres positioned relative to the head joint.

I'm placing the eyes forward on the face, then adding a small bird perched on top of the head with its own joint hierarchy (body, wings) parented to the head, plus a stub tail and tiny teeth, all assembled using the part helper with bone and position arguments and mottled fur coloring.
